commentary_segments.text: This circuit contains mainly one single-transistor amplifier. How can we set the average output voltage without feedback on this transistor? The answer is replica biasing. A transistor with the same characteristics is put in parallel. This one is now part of a feedback loop. Its DC output voltage will be V . The average output REF voltage of the amplifier itself will also be V . REF The DC output voltage will not be exactly V of course, because some mismatch is always REF present. The capacitance is required to reduce the influence of the AC voltage on the biasing. The resistor R is to raise the AC input impedance of the amplifier. S
